symptom: The committed TypeScript test embedded a one-backslash newline escape in a Python bytes literal, so the generated Python child source contained an actual newline inside a single-quoted literal. Both new FD-lifetime tests failed with SyntaxError before executing any kernel or FD assertion; verify exited 1 while research-governance passed and post-checkout succeeded. Local success had used a different correctly escaped source file.
lesson: When Python source is embedded inside TypeScript string literals, a one-backslash newline escape is interpreted by JavaScript before Python sees the code and may create an unterminated Python bytes literal. A locally passing file does not verify a differently escaped committed file. Inspect the complete child stderr and the exact repository-read-back source before attributing red CI to the research mechanism.
guardrail: Do not rerun the unchanged one-backslash embedded Python fixture. Preserve two backslashes in TypeScript source when Python must receive a literal backslash-n; validate the generated child program and read back the committed source. Attribute test syntax, process exit, workflow conclusion, post-job and runner separately; never call a kernel/FD research method failed when its child never parsed. Keep productionConnection false and no protected N2 or Current BUY/LINE/public/production changes.
